author: haiku
label: c2-seed-haiku-01
changes: Added a summary, a terms list and the device state keys, so each term is defined once.
Defined the server contract: start returns start_seq, the page and changes endpoints with their sizes, and that each product carries its change_seq, which the apply rule needs.
Replaced the one-line steps with five numbered steps, each giving its trigger, what it does, the data it moves, where state is kept and what happens on failure.
Saved the cursor and catch_up_seq in the same transaction as each page or batch, so a kill mid-page resumes cleanly.
Defined the swap as one SQLite transaction, with a retry at the next launch or foreground if it fails.
Added the apply rule (change_seq comparison), which the first version named but did not define.
Defined the 410 path: a re-download into staging while products keeps serving reps, and a full restart when catch-up hits 410.
Restored the brief's Wi-Fi pause, retry timing (2, 4, 8, 16 s), 5-attempt limit and next-trigger rule, which the first version had dropped or only named.
Decided that incremental sync pauses during a full download, so only one writer touches the catalogue.
Kept the first-download browsing question open, as the brief requires, and added two further open questions the brief leaves unstated.
Summary reduced to a short description of today's system, the flow and the reason for staging; the flow itself is no longer repeated in the summary.

Terms: added catch_up_seq, last_seq and sync_state with the meaning of mode (full until swap, incremental otherwise); defined HTTP 410 as this plan's choice because the brief says only 'resync required'.
Endpoints: stated that the full endpoint returns live products (assumed, listed as an open question) and that 410 is returned for a window overrun.
Apply rule: stated that a product with no local row is inserted and a tombstone with no row does nothing; the rule now says 'no row or higher change_seq'.
Wi-Fi rule: the start call is included, since the brief says the full download runs only on Wi-Fi.
One writer: now states that incremental sync does not run while mode is full, answering the 410 hand-off question.
Step 1: trigger now defined by sync_state (no row, or mode full without start_seq); catch_up_seq is set to start_seq; a 410 clears start_seq and cursor.
Step 2: added launch and Wi-Fi-return triggers for a paused download; an empty page moves to step 3 so a resume after the last page works.
Step 3: added the explanation of why catch-up fixes rows fetched during edits; a killed app resumes at step 2 and then catches up from catch_up_seq.

Step 4: last_seq is now catch_up_seq instead of the larger of start_seq and catch_up_seq, since catch_up_seq never starts below start_seq; swap clears catch_up_seq; added the open-read handling; the swap-failure retry now re-runs catch-up, so it needs Wi-Fi and network, which corrects the earlier no-network claim.
Step 5: a 410 sets mode to full and goes to step 1; last_attempt_at is set at the start so failed attempts count toward the 15-minute throttle; the launch-within-15-minutes case is stated.
Failure handling kept in each step as the brief requires; the separate failure section now only points to them, so nothing is said twice.
Open questions: added whether the full endpoint omits tombstones and whether the SQLite driver blocks the swap during an open read; the existing three questions are kept.
Step 3's 410 now also clears start_seq, so step 1 runs on the re-download. Before, start_seq stayed set and the skip rule in step 1 would have skipped the re-download, contradicting step 5.
Apply rule now states that a tombstone with no stored row changes nothing and is not stored (Q17).
Step 2: an empty cursor means the first page, and the trigger includes return to the foreground, matching the retry rule and the step 4 failure path.
Step 3: explains that a product deleted before start_seq and re-created later comes back from catch-up as a plain insert (Q16).
Step 4: the swap waits for open catalogue reads to close, then reruns steps 2 and 3 before swapping. The app tracks its own reads (Q18).
Step 5: Wi-Fi returning does not trigger incremental sync, and the next trigger is the first launch or foreground event at least 15 minutes after last_attempt_at (Q20).
New 'How the sync runs' section: one routine picks the step from sync_state and runs only in the foreground (Q21).
Retry rule stated once. Per-step failure text now covers only what differs, and a short cross-step table replaces the repeated failure notes.
Open questions: added the stale-catalogue notice after a 410 (Q19) and background running (Q21).
Rewrote the whole document once for a newcomer, in the required order: summary, terms, steps, failures, open questions. No stated requirement, limit, number or rule was dropped.
Summary now first says how the system works today (Postgres sequence stamps, SQLite holding only settings), then what the app will do, in four short sentences. Dropped the second telling of the flow.

Defined the terms a newcomer needs: change_seq, tombstone and tombstone window, keyset pagination, resync required with the 410 note, products, products_staging, swap, mode, start_seq, cursor, catch_up_seq, last_seq and last_attempt_at. Added a short 'reading sync_state' list covering first run, unfinished download, re-download needed and complete catalogue.
Added a 'Server endpoints' section so the three endpoints are defined before the steps that call them, and a 'How the sync runs' section on the single routine that picks the step.

Rules used by several steps are kept as four named rules (apply, retry, Wi-Fi, one writer). The apply rule's tombstone case is stated plainly. The 'page and cursor saved together' and 'start_seq taken before the first page' reasons now sit in the steps they apply to, not in a separate rule.

Each step has the same four parts: trigger, what it does, data kept, and failure. The step 3 catch-up correctness argument is kept as a short 'Why this is enough' list inside step 3, with the deleted-then-re-created case reworded so it does not depend on an unexplained term.

Merged repeated failure text: the 'resumes from cursor' and 'swap needs Wi-Fi' statements now appear once in their step, and the failure table repeats only the situation and the resume point, in plain words.
Kept all seven open questions from the first version, reworded in plain sentences, with no references to other items. The browse-during-first-download question is still marked as not decided.
Added no new mechanism. The 15-minute throttle, the 410 handling and the swap wait are the same as the first version, now stated in one place each.
holes: Q19: During a re-download after a 410, mode is full, so incremental sync is off. How long can reps be on a stale products table, and do they see anything telling them the catalogue is out of date? (author: How long reps stay on the stale table is not known. It runs from the 410 until the re-download swaps in, which can take hours and waits for Wi-Fi. The plan shows reps no out-of-date notice, and whether product wants one is not decided. Listed under Open questions.)
